docs.title: Editable Strings (UIString) API
docs.text: This document outlines how to use the Editable Strings (UIString) API to manage translations for the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The UIString feature allows for dynamic management of strings in the application's UI. Strings are stored as key-value pairs, with support for English and Arabic translations. The API provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting these strings.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All API endpoints require authentication. You must have the EDIT_UI_STRINGS permission to create, update, or delete UI strings.

docs.title: Retrieve a UI String
docs.text:
• GET /api/strings/{key}/

    Retrieves a single UI string by its key.

    Parameters:

    • key (string): The key of the UI string to retrieve.
    • lang (string, optional): The language to retrieve. Can be en or ar. Defaults to en.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/?lang=ar"

    Example Response:

    json { "title": "مرحباً", "body": "مرحباً بك في تطبيقنا!" }

docs.title: Create a UI String
docs.text:
• POST /api/strings/

    Creates a new UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "new_feature_announcement", "values_en": { "title": "New Feature!", "description": "We have a new feature for you to try." }, "values_ar": { "title": "ميزة جديدة!", "description": "لدينا ميزة جديدة لتجربتها." } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/"

docs.title: Update a UI String
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/strings/{key}/

    Updates an existing UI string.

    Example Request (PUT):

    bash curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "welcome_message", "values_en": { "title": "Welcome", "body": "Welcome to our app!" }, "values_ar": { "title": "أهلاً بك", "body": "أهلاً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

    Example Request (PATCH):

    bash curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "values_en": { "title": "Welcome Back", "body": "Welcome back to our app!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Delete a UI String
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/strings/{key}/

    Deletes a UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
• values_ar can be empty or null.
  • If values_ar is not empty, it must have the exact same keys as values_en. An empty JSON object ({}) is also acceptable.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
This API uses a concept of dynamically defined permissions, which can be edited via the Django Admin interface. This page is intended simply to explain the concept in general terms. Pages focusing on specific features or areas of the API will go into further detail on the specific permissions relevant to those endpoints.

The permissions for API endpoints are controlled to some extent by hard-coded logic (e.g. trip lead can edit a trip), but also in many cases through the PermissionMatrix model. This model is intended to be edited only via Django Admin interface, with read-only API endpoints available for clients to determine permissions that apply for an authenticated user.

The PermissionMatrix model contains 3 properties as shown below, with subsequent sections explaining purpose of each in more detail:

docs.title: Action (required)
docs.text:
The action column indicates which permission the entity/row relates to.

The full list of ActionChoice options can be fetched via the api/choices/permissionmatrixaction endpoint, but include things like CREATE_TRIP, CREATE_TRIP_WITH_APPROVAL and APPROVE_TRIP.

docs.title: Levels (optional)
docs.text:
The levels column indicates which levels the permission applies to. It is possible to select multiple levels. For trips this would be e.g. the level of that trip, while for upgrade request it would be the level that the applicant is requesting to be upgraded to.

If left blank, the permission applies to ALL levels.

For some actions the levels field has no effect. In those cases that will be indicated through the name of the action in the Django Admin interface.

docs.title: Group (required)
docs.text: The group column indicates which groups the permission applies to. All members of the group will be granted the permission to perform the action for the appropriate levels.

docs.title: Usage in backend code
docs.text:
The views (endpoints) make use of these permissions mainly via the permission_classes property of a django-rest-framework viewset, e.g. as seen in this example:

from api.permissions import CanCreateTripPermission

class TripCreateView(generics.CreateAPIView):
    queryset = Trip.objects.all()
    serializer_class = CreateTripSerializer
    permission_classes = [CanCreateTripPermission]

docs.title: Accepting Members from Waiting List
docs.text:
When a member cancels their registration to a trip, the member first in line on waiting list will automatically be added to the registered list.

Trip lead, deputy leads and any member with 'EDITTRIPREGISTRATIONS' permission can accept a specific member from waitlist to the registered list via the /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist endpoint. This will ignore trip capacity, allowing the count of registered members to exceed the trip capacity.
